coterie_cantor.name: The Horned Priest — Choir Aspect
coterie_cantor.prompt: Replace the previous serpent Priest concept with a new original creature concept using the TWO user-supplied horror reference illustrations: the mouth-covered humanoid and the enormous sinewy flesh idol. The previous snake priest illustration is only a reference for costume continuity. Create ONE complete adult humanoid dark-fantasy boss called the Horned Priest — Choir Aspect. A hunched, towering malformed humanoid silhouette, broad asymmetric upper torso and a bulky fused shoulder-neck mass crowded with several tooth-lined animal jaws and murmuring mouths of different sizes. One dominant howling maw replaces the face, with secondary mouths across neck and chest; there should be no recognizable snake head, serpent coils or snake tail. Pale grey-green scarred skin, dark burgundy folds, knotted sinews, thin trailing tendrils and ragged wrappings, presented as a painted fictional monster rather than realistic exposed organs. Two long uneven arms with curled claw hands; two weight-bearing humanoid or beastlike legs, visible feet grounded on the same level. Preserve the same Priest identity: remnants of a deep charcoal ecclesiastical coat with torn burgundy lining hanging off the body, rusted circular iron gorget, black obsidian pendant, bone trophies and a hanging censer. A jagged rune at the breastbone glows faintly icy blue, many mouths caught singing one unnatural hymn. Readable side-view or three-quarter LEFT facing game silhouette, dynamic but stationary combat-ready pose. Combine the references' anatomical invention into an original design, do not reproduce their exact characters or composition. Match the existing game concepts' rough dark ink contours, angular painted shading, muted colours, worn iron and bone details. Keep luminous pale midtones for readability. Full creature visible, generous empty margin around EVERY hand, head, foot and tendril; no cropped anatomy. One isolated creature only on genuine alpha TRANSPARENT background; no scenery, no grey studio backdrop, no vignette, no cast shadow, no ground plane, no smaller figures, no text or watermark.
